checks.description: the cluster is ACTIVE on Kubernetes 1.37
checks.because: Terraform created one EKS Auto Mode cluster at the pinned minor version.

checks.description: the database is available, Multi-AZ, with a standby in a different zone
checks.because: One PostgreSQL instance holds the engine's histories and the session database. RDS keeps a synchronous standby in another zone.

checks.description: the engine runs two frontend, two history and two matching pods, and one worker service pod
checks.because: Temporal's chart is installed with two replicas of each stateful service, so losing one pod is survivable (S10).

checks.description: the engine reports itself serving, on PostgreSQL for both histories and search
checks.because: The server answers on its own API and names its two stores.

checks.description: two stateless workers, and two each of the model gateway, tool gateway, session API and sandbox manager, are ready
checks.because: Each is a Deployment. Workers hold no run; the gateways keep their state in the database.

checks.description: no component keeps state on a volume
checks.because: Everything a run needs is in the engine's database, the session database or S3. Replacing a pod loses nothing.

checks.description: every tool is classified: local, read-only, idempotent, checkable or unsafe
checks.because: The class is part of a tool's registration in the gateway. It decides how a retry of the same step is made safe (S05).

checks.description: no sandbox exists while no run needs one
checks.because: A sandbox is created for a step that needs files and deleted while a run waits.

checks.description: the workers' autoscaler watches the engine's task queue, not CPU
checks.because: KEDA's Temporal scaler reads each task queue's backlog from the engine (S11).
